final_text:
first roll forward to the next business day, then count n business days after that (same counting semantics as before).
    - n < 0: if start is a non-business day, first roll backward to the previous business day, then count |n| business days backward.
    - Weekends and any dates in holidays are skipped identical to weekends.
  - business_days_between(a, b, holidays=()): returns count of business days in [a, b). If b < a returns negative of business_days_between(b, a).
- invoices.py
  - due_date(issued, terms, holidays=()): accepts optional holidays and passes them to add_business_days.

Notes and examples
- Signature highlights:
  - is_business_day(d, holidays=())
  - add_business_days(start, n, holidays=())
  - business_days_between(a, b, holidays=())
  - invoices.due_date(issued, terms, holidays=())
- Example behavior:
  - add_business_days(date(2026,10,9), 1) => next business day after 2026-10-09 (counts forward excluding start) 
  - add_business_days(date(2026,10,10), -1) => start on Saturday, rolls back to Friday then counts one business day back -> Thursday
  - business_days_between(a, b) counts business days including a and excluding b
